items.title: TCI Express to invest ₹500 crore in 5 years to expand logistics infra
items.rss_summary: Logistics solutions company TCI Express Ltd on Thursday announced a Rs 500-crore infrastructure expansion plan for the next five years and the opening of three sorting centres in Ahmedabad, Lucknow and Kolkata, strengthening its nationwide express delivery network. Through these strategic investments, the company said it aims to build a future-ready logistics ecosystem, enhance service capabilities and reinforce its position as one of India's leading players in the sector. The company said it has already invested Rs 500 crore in the last seven years, and now intends to direct the new investment to high-performing verticals. "We are witnessing strong growth momentum across our business verticals, particularly domestic air express and e-commerce express, which have emerged as key growth drivers in FY2027. Our next phase of expansion will focus on strengthening the capabilities of individual verticals, enhancing operational efficiencies and building a more agile and scalable network,"

items.title: Rupee slides 8 paise to 93.49 against US dollar during early trade
items.rss_summary: The rupee slipped 8 paise to 93.49 against the US dollar in early trade on Thursday, weighed down by a strong greenback and weak domestic equity markets. However, lower crude oil prices and foreign-fund inflows capped the rupee's fall, forex traders said. At the interbank foreign exchange market, the rupee opened at 93.40 and declined to 93.49 against the greenback, registering a loss of 8 paise from its previous close. The domestic currency climbed 10 paise to close at 93.41 against US dollar on Wednesday after gaining 68 paise in the preceding two sessions. "The decline in crude prices and RBI's actions to curb speculative activity in the currency have helped the rupee gain strength. In the near-term, the rupee is likely to trade in the 93.20 to 94 range," said V K Vijayakumar, Chief Investment Strategist, Geojit Investments. According to Kaveri More, Commodity Technical Analyst at Choice Broking, the rupee was supported by foreign equity inflows and softer crude oil prices. ...

items.title: Tata Sons board members to visit Air India HQ, review performance on Nov 19
items.rss_summary: Tata Sons board members, including Chairman N Chandrasekaran and Noel Tata, will be visiting Air India headquarters in Gurugram on Thursday, according to sources. Air India is co-owned by Tata Sons and Singapore Airlines, which holds a 25.1 per cent stake. The sources said the members will be reviewing the performance of the loss-making Air India. The airline's MD and CEO Tewolde Gebremariam will be making a presentation to the members, they added. Besides, operational integration of Air India and Air India Express is likely to be discussed, the sources said. Tata Sons Chairman Chandrasekaran, board member Noel Tata and others will be visiting the Air India headquarters on Thursday, they added. It could not be immediately ascertained whether all the Tata Sons board members will be visiting the airline's headquarters.
